articles.title: Villarreal - PSG | El peor rival, en el peor momento
articles.standfirst: El submarino recibe al mejor equipo de Europa entre las dudas tras la derrota ante el Espanyol
articles.summary: El submarino recibe al mejor equipo de Europa entre las dudas tras la derrota ante el Espanyol
articles.body: El Villarreal afronta este martes una de las citas que esta temporada estaba marcada en rojo en su calendario particular. La visita del PSG, actual campeón de Europa, a La Cerámica siempre debería ser motivo de fiesta para una hinchada como la azulejera. Pero el contexto en este momento es otro bien diferente y no invita a excesivas alegrías. La reciente derrota liguera ante el Espanyol ha hecho mucho daño en Vila-real. Y ya no tanto por los puntos perdidos como por la sensación de volver a la casilla de salida para un equipo comenzaba a mostrar claros síntomas de recuperación en las últimas jornadas. Las dudas que parecían disiparse han surgido de nuevo y con más virulencia si cabe. Los nubarrones vuelven a revolotear sobre La Cerámica, escenario en el que el Villarreal está dando su peor imagen esta temporada. Y sucede justo cuando llega el peor invitado posible en el peor momento de la temporada. Con bajas de futbolistas de peso y experiencia, caso de Juan Foyth y Gerard Moreno, cualquier opción amarilla pasa por transformación radical en tiempo récord para ofrecer la mejor versión de la temporada. Esa que por momentos dio ante rivales como Dortmund, Nápoles o Liverpool, pero aumentado su cadencia y continuidad. Los 40 minutos buenos en Anfield pueden invitar a la esperanza como las buenas sensaciones en Alemania. Pero a todas luces son insuficientes para competir ante el mejor equipo de la competición si no se dan durante casi todo el partido, con la dificultad innegable que ello entraña. Nadie dijo que medirse a este PSG fuera fácil. Siempre quedarán los optimistas que vean en la de esta noche la oportunidad perfecta para disipar los nubarrones con un triunfo de prestigio ante el gran favorito al título. Hasta la fecha se ha visto un Villarreal de dos caras diferentes. La del equipo incapaz cuando en casa ha tenido que llevar el peso de los encuentros (tan sólo 4 puntos de 15 en Liga) y el equipo compacto y competitivo que, más allá de resultados, ha dado la cara en escenarios como Anfield, Dortmund, Bernabéu o Metropolitano. Todo hace indicar que, dado el contexto actual y el tipo de rival, ante los de Luis Enrique la intención sea la de apostar por el Villarreal de visita en grandes escenarios, aunque lo haga como local. El regreso de Saliba refuerza la posibilidad del trivote, toda vez que se busque la velocidad en ataque buscando la sorpresa ante la posibilidad de tener mayores espacios. Tras un inicio dubitativo de temporada, el PSG ya recuerda al que ha dominado la Champions con puño de hierro. Los dos empates y la derrota con la que comenzaron la temporada en la Ligue 1, al margen de la derrota en la Supercopa francesa ante el Lens, han dado paso a una racha de nueve victorias consecutivas en la que los parisinos han descargado su furia con 30 goles anotados y contundentes victorias en Champions ante el Slovan (6-1), City (2-4) y Barcelona (4-2). Las ausencias de Marquinhos, Kvaratskhelia y Dembelé no han hecho más que demostrar la profundidad de plantilla de un equipo que ha encontrado en Akliouche y Mika Godts recambios de garantías.

articles.title: Atlético - Bayern: El balón es Oro para el Atleti
articles.standfirst: Harry Kane, como mejor futbolista del planeta, desafía la posesión, el toque y las combinaciones corales con las que los de Simeone presentan su candidatura a todo
articles.summary: Harry Kane, como mejor futbolista del planeta, desafía la posesión, el toque y las combinaciones corales con las que los de Simeone presentan su candidatura a todo
articles.body: Se estrena como visitante en el Metropolitano un Harry Kane que desafía al Atlético con su condición de mejor futbolista del planeta. Sin embargo, el Balón también es Oro para los de Simeone, que en su enésima reinvención, construye un equipo aspirante a todo a través del toque y la posesión. No falta el innegociable trabajo que también ha llevado al inglés a imponer los valores de la humildad, la constancia y el bien del colectivo por encima del marketing y el ego individual, pero la tropa rojiblanca que persigue el top 8 de la Champions y que se juega el liderato de LaLiga el domingo impone con un estilo propositivo y protagonista tanto como los grandes a los que mira a los ojos. Valgan como referencia los 12 partidos del Atlético de los 14 disputados en los que superó en posesión a su oponente (incluidos el 61-39% registrado frente al Real Madrid en el derbi o el 29-71% con que forjó su victoria frente al Espanyol en el RCDE Stadium) o los goles tras combinaciones corales de más de 20 toques que dibujó en el Pizjuán, en Anfield, en la visita del eterno rival al Metropolitano o por última vez el pasado sábado en el Ciutat de Valencia. Una confianza y seguridad con el balón (con un Barrios listo para comandar también a la España campeona del mundo y con un Baena que tras cinco goles y cuatro asistencias empieza a emular las genialidades de Griezmann) que se postula como el mayor argumento para restar brillo a Kane y a un Olise renqueante en un Bayern mermado por lo físico. No obstante, la ausencia del Cuti también impide uno de los mayores duelos que se pueden presenciar a día de hoy entre un delantero y un central. Más allá de las bajas con las que se presentan dos de los semifinalistas de la pasada edición de la Champions (las ausencias de Cardoso y Hjulmand condicionan el centro del campo rojiblanco), si hay alguien que ha conseguido convertir en terrenal al Bayern ese no es otro que El Cholo. Odiado por el Atlético desde el maldito gol de Schwarzenbeck en el desempate de la final de 1974, al gigante alemán se le atragantan las visitas a Madrid desde que Simeone habita en el banquillo. En la primera asistió al maradoniano eslalon de Saúl en el Calderón que ya no sería capaz de remontar el cuadro de Guardiola en Múnich para sellar su billete hacia la final de Milán de 2016, en la segunda sucumbiría con un gol de Carrasco en la fase de grupos y sólo el punto cosechado en la liguilla de 2020 (1-1) impidió que en su tercera visita, ya al Metropolitano, también se fuera de vacío.

articles.title: El Barcelona levanta el castigo a la grada de animación ante el Aston Villa
articles.standfirst: Luz verde a la grada de animación en Champions pese a los incidentes del Clásico —con intento de agresión a Camavinga— y la denuncia de LaLiga
articles.summary: Luz verde a la grada de animación en Champions pese a los incidentes del Clásico —con intento de agresión a Camavinga— y la denuncia de LaLiga
articles.body: Tras la reunión celebrada hoy entre representantes de las áreas del club responsables de la gestión de la grada de animación y los portavoces de los diferentes grupos que forman parte de ella, el Barcelona ha decidido levantar la suspensión cautelar. Los 1200 integrantes de la grada de animación se habían quedado fuera del choque ante el Alavés después de los incidentes protagonizados por algunos aficionados durante el clásico contra el Real Madrid, que han provocado denuncias por parte de la Liga ante los organismos disciplinarios de la Real Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF). LaLiga trasladó a la RFEF un informe que detallaba hasta diez incidentes protagonizados por aficionados azulgranas. Entre los hechos recogidos figuran insultos dirigidos a figuras como José Mourinho y Marc Cucurella, así como el lanzamiento de diversos objetos al terreno de juego, tales como botellas, latas y mecheros. Asimismo, el informe destacó un grave intento de agresión contra el jugador del Real Madrid Eduardo Camavinga, a quien habrían tratado de golpear con el mástil de una bandera durante la celebración del segundo gol del conjunto blanco. Ahora, los portavoces se han comprometido a velar por un comportamiento cívico y respetuoso en la grada. El club da así un voto de confianza a este grupo de seguidores, que tiene un papel importante a la hora de dar apoyo al equipo durante todo el partido. El club realizará un seguimiento estricto del cumplimiento de este compromiso. Las conductas que motivaron la suspensión ya han comportado sanciones económicas reiteradas y exponen al club incluso al riesgo de clausura del estadio. El Barcelona confía en que, con el compromiso de todos, estas situaciones no se volverán a producir, en beneficio de los socios y socias, del conjunto de la afición y de la entidad.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin Laments End of LSU-Alabama Yearly Rivalry Game, 'Really Come Down to Money'
articles.summary: Alabama and LSU have faced each other every year since 1964, but that will change during the 2027 college football season.
articles.body:
Alabama and LSU have faced each other every year since 1964, but that will change during the 2027 college football season.

And LSU head coach Lane Kiffin isn't happy about it.

"I think that's just sad," Kiffin said Monday, per ESPN's Alex Scarborough . "And I understand, so I'm not being critical. All the decisions, usually, I think all of them probably really come down to money, whether that's the realignments, whether that's the rivalries. So, I think it's all sad in general in the big picture of things that money drives to make [changes to] such great traditions and rivalries.

"And there's really good things that have changed in college football over the years, but there's also a lot that I think myself and a lot of people wish that they were the way that they were, rivalries and conferences the same. And so unfortunately it's where we are that really doesn't seem like much is going to be protected when it comes to TV contracts and money and other people's ideas."

As Scarborough explained, the SEC designated three permanent rivals for each team in anticipation of moving to a nine-game conference schedule. Alabama and LSU were not named as permanent rivals, meaning they will not face each other next year but will play in 2028 and at least once every two years following.

Alabama's permanent rivals are Auburn, Mississippi State and Tennessee, while LSU's are Texas A&M, Arkansas and Ole Miss.

The Crimson Tide have longstanding traditional rivalry games with Auburn and Tennessee, while Mississippi State is approximately 90 miles away. Geography clearly played a role in the decision to include the Bulldogs.

Kiffin is familiar with the games between LSU and Alabama from the latter's side, as he was the Crimson Tide's offensive coordinator from 2014 through 2016 under head coach Nick Saban. Saban himself was LSU's head coach for five seasons before he built Alabama into the gold standard of college football during his 17 years at the helm.

That such a notable figure as Saban coached for both sides elevated the rivalry.

As for Kiffin, Saturday's game will be his first against the Crimson Tide as the head coach of LSU. The stakes couldn't be much higher, as the winner will be in solid College Football Playoff position, while the loser will have three losses and likely be on the outside looking in ahead of the stretch run.

articles.title: Harry Kane: Bayern Munich striker would swap Ballon d'Or trophy for Champions League winner's medal
articles.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane says he would swap his Ballon d'Or trophy for a Champions League winner's medal.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane says he would swap his Ballon d'Or trophy for a Champions League winner's medal.

The 33-year-old became the first Englishman since 2001 to win the accolade , beating Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal.

But Kane, who is expected to sign a new contract with Bayern "within the next few days", says winning Europe's elite club competition is at the forefront of his mind after a "rollercoaster" week.

"Team trophies are why we play football. The team aspect of our sport is really, really important," Kane told a news conference before Bayern's Champions League fixture with Atletico Madrid in the Spanish capital.

"The Ballon d'Or last week was one of the best feelings I've had in my life and my career.

"But to have moments with the team, celebrations with the club - to be able to lift the Champions League with Bayern would be an incredible feeling."

When asked if he had to pick between lifting the European Cup and the Ballon d'Or, the England captain added: "I would choose the Champions League, but I have the opportunity to do both - let's see what happens.

"The Ballon d'Or is a highlight, it puts me on an even bigger level, but you want to have these big finals, the Champions League, having that feeling of emotion with your team-mates as well."

Kane was feted at the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London, becoming just the fifth Englishman to win the award, joining Michael Owen, Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton and Kevin Keegan on an elite list.

Bayern and their supporters also paid tribute to Kane before Saturday's Der Klassiker against Borussia Dortmund.

The Bavarian club have not had a Ballon d'Or winner since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge claimed the award in 1981.

"It's been a rollercoaster since the celebrations," said Kane, who scored 73 goals for club and country last season as he helped Bayern win a domestic treble.

"It was a huge high for me, but also for the club. It was one of the best feelings I've ever had in my life, without a doubt.

"But we've had some lows and a lot of extremes we've had to deal with. It's brought us closer together and we fight for every moment."

Ranking England's Ballon d'Or winners - how does Kane compare?

How Kane defied doubters to become world's best

Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or wait - how he bucked the trend

Kane said there had been "good conversations" in recent days over a new contract with Bayern and he was "extremely close" to putting pen to paper on a deal.

"A lot of the bigger stuff has been ironed out and we are happy with," said Kane, who joined Bayern from Tottenham for £86.4m (100m euros) in August 2023.

"But in every contract there are loads of little things that go into it, small details that in the end the lawyers have to thrash out and figure out.

"So all in all I would say it is more days than weeks. From what I have heard, the conversations have gone well again today.

"Hopefully we will be in a place to do something within the next few days."

Bayern's preparations have also been overshadowed by the absence of head coach Vincent Kompany.

The Belgian was taken to hospital after collapsing during a training session involving Bayern's reserve team on 23 October.

Kompany was discharged from hospital five days later and is continuing his recovery, with no definitive return date established.

Assistant Aaron Danks has overseen first-team duties in his absence.

Kane acknowledged the difficulty of being without his manager but insisted the squad were coping well.

"We're missing our coach, but everyone has the opportunity to prove themselves and there's a long way to go," he added.

articles.title: El Mallorca se aferra a Son Moix y aprende a remontar... a cabezazo limpio
articles.standfirst: Dio buena imagen, mereció ganar más holgado y voltean el gol de Antonio Cordero con sendos testarazos de Pablo Torre y Adri Fuentes para la primera remontada del curso
articles.summary: Dio buena imagen, mereció ganar más holgado y voltean el gol de Antonio Cordero con sendos testarazos de Pablo Torre y Adri Fuentes para la primera remontada del curso
articles.body: Un gol en el último suspiro de Adri Fuentes le sirve al Mallorca para doblegar al Cádiz en Son Moix, donde ha ganado cinco de sus seis citas, tras un partido que dominó casi de principio a fin, pero en el que perdonó mucho. Antoñito Cordero adelantó a un buen equipo gaditano, pero los cabezazos de Pablo Torre y Adri Fuentes le valen al Mallorca para regresar a zona de 'playoffs'. Por su parte, los andaluces vuelven a caer a puestos de descenso. Empezaba agresivo el Mallorca en los primeros minutos con una primera ocasión nada mas arrancar el encuentro de Adrián Liso a pase de Pablo Torre. Una tónica que seguiría durante prácticamente toda la primera parte con todo tipo de oportunidades para los bermellones que no se transformaron en gol. Antes del primer cuarto de hora un doble remate, primero de Zito Luvumbo y, posteriormente, de Adri Fuentes se perdían para el Mallorca y blocaba Jokin Ezquieta. El ariete madrileño gozaba de otro remate claro pasada la media hora, donde no conseguía ajustar bien el remate de cabeza que se marchaba fuera por poco. Pero la ocasión más clara del encuentro la tenía Zito Luvumbo en el minuto 35 con un envío tenso de Liso desde el costado izquierdo que llegaba al segundo palo e, incompresiblemente, la mandaba fuera con la portería vacía. Una primera parte donde el Cádiz apenas se ha acercado a la portería de Arnau Tenas, mas allá de un disparo lejano de Borja Vázquez que se marchaba muy desviado y un gol anulado al propio Borja por falta previa sobre Raíllo. El Mallorca arrancaba en la misma línea la segunda mitad, con una ocasión de Liso, cuyo remate cruzado se marchó fuera por poco, y una gran acción individual de Pablo Torre, con caño incluido, cuyo disparo desde la frontal sacaba Ezkieta metiendo una mano prodigiosa. Sin embargo, los visitantes golpeaban a renglón seguido, cuando Antoñito Cordero marcaba en una transición con un remate con el exterior ajustado al poste tras hacer la pared con Dilan Zárate. Incluso Ukwuije pudo hacer el segundo al cabecear un córner de Antoñito, mientras el equipo bermellón insistía, pero Liso estrellaba el balón en el palo. Finalmente el premio llegaba superada la hora de partido cuando Pablo Torre acabó logrando el empate al cabecear en plancha el centro con la izquierda de Zito Luvumbo. Son Moix se impacientaba con varias decisiones arbitrales, pero también con las imprecisiones de los suyos, especialmente de un Adri Fuentes poco fino con el balón en los pies. Y fue precisamente el delantero centro bermellón quien aparecía en el minuto 89 para rematar de cabeza, también lanzándose en plancha, un gran balón de Álex Sala, que cerraba así su gran encuentro. Adri fuentes terminaba desatando la alegría en Son Moix y culminando la remontada: una victoria justa para el Mallorca.

articles.title: El Deportivo vuelve a ganar en el regreso de Aubameyang
articles.standfirst: La milagrosa recuperación del gabonés impulsa al Deportivo a una sufrida remontada ante Osasuna con goles de Soriano y Nsongo
articles.summary: La milagrosa recuperación del gabonés impulsa al Deportivo a una sufrida remontada ante Osasuna con goles de Soriano y Nsongo
articles.body: Volvió Aubameyang a Riazor y el Deportivo volvió a ganar. No marcó el gabonés, pero su recuperación milagrosa y presencia iluminó a su equipo tras siete jornadas sin sumar de tres. En el 87’ remontaron a un Osasuna, ramplón y conformista, que no ha encontrado el efecto esperado con el cambio de entrenador. Se adelantó sin merecer, pero se vio superado de forma merecida en un segundo acto de pasión deportivista. Deportivo comenzó afilado y con Yeremay fallando goles. El extremo canario perdonó dos ocasiones clarísimas en sendos mano a mano nacidos de la fragilidad defensiva de Osasuna. El primero llegó tras un error grosero de Boyomo, blando en la disputa, que entregó la posesión y dejó a Yeremay solo ante Sergio Herrera; sin embargo, el atacante erró en último control y desajustado no pudo con el portero rival. Pocos minutos después, fue Catena quien se dejó robar la pelota en zona prohibida, pero el punta del Depor volvió a estrellarse contra un inconmensurable meta rojillo, que se le echó encima cerrando todos los espacios. Herrera se mostraba inspiradísimo en su retorno a la titularidad. Después, Mella cabeceaba un nuevo aviso para firmar la tercera ocasión consecutiva de un Deportivo que sometía a placer a un Osasuna de plastilina en Riazor. Otra de Mella, con un tiro raso lamiendo el palo, reafirmó el entusiasmo gallego en un choque intenso, pero falto de finura a la hora de matar. Solo un error capital cambió la dinámica. Osasuna vivía en un sobresalto continuo, pero tiene a Budimir. El croata también abusó de la defensa del Depor, que siempre encaja. Leo Román regaló el gol con un error increíble. Sin presión dio la pelota a Dubasin, este cedió a Moi, que vio a Budimir y ya. Ocho goles en LaLiga para el punta balcánico de 35 años. El Deportivo no ganaba desde el 5 de septiembre y su entrenador buscó mordiente tras el descanso. Adama y Aubameyang a jugar para dominar todo el segundo acto. El Depor mandaba, pero no inquietaba, hasta que una falta sobre Yeremay los metió en el partido. Soriano le pegó rasa y fuerte, superó la barrera y Sergio Herrera tocó, pero no pudo despejar, dejando la sensación de que podía hacer más. En otra falta lateral, Luismi Cruz se sacó una comba que pudo poner en ventaja al Deportivo. Osasuna estaba siendo superado y no mostraba capacidad para reaccionar. El Deportivo insistía y metía miedo con Nsongo y las continuas internadas de Altimira... y se reservó lo mejor para el final. Ganó con un gol de puro músculo. Adama ganó la línea de fondo por pura potencia, Auba saltó mucho más que su marcador para cabecear y Nsongo fue un rayo para rematar el rechace que dejó Sergio Herrera tras un paradón. Osambela la tuvo de cabeza en otro horror defensivo local, pero el larguero evitó un empate rojillo que hubiera resultado inmerecido. La noche que regresó Aubameyang, el Deportivo volvió a ganar en LaLiga.

articles.title: El mensaje de Caparrós a Pepe Mel: "Este partido lo vas a ganar seguro"
articles.standfirst: El ex técnico verdiblanco fue operado tras sufrir un accidente vascular cerebral
articles.summary: El ex técnico verdiblanco fue operado tras sufrir un accidente vascular cerebral
articles.body: Joaquín Caparrós y el Sevilla se han sumado a los numerosos mensajes de ánimo y cariño que ha recibido Pepe Mel de aficionados, clubes y compañeros en las últimas horas. El que fuera técnico de equipos como el Tenerife y el Betis, al que entrenó en dos etapas y en una de ellas lo devolvió a Primera, pasó por quirófano este domingo en la capital hispalense tras sufrir un accidente cerebrovascular en su domicilio. "Querido Pepe, toda mi fuerza y mis mejores deseos para una pronta recuperación. Eres un profesional y un luchador ejemplar dentro y fuera de los terrenos de juego. Este partido lo vas a ganar seguro. Un abrazo muy fuerte", escribió Caparrós, que también se recupera de una grave enfermedad, en sus redes sociales. Clubes como Almería, Málaga, Deportivo, Las Palmas, Real Madrid, West Bromwich o Alavés lanzaron sus mensajes de apoyo hacia el ex verdiblanco. También lo ha hecho el club de Nervión. "El Sevilla FC desea enviar un mensaje de apoyo a Pepe Mel y su familia y le trasladamos nuestros mejores deseos para que tenga una pronta recuperación. ¡Mucho ánimo!", escribió el club sevillista.

articles.title: Oklahoma fires offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle, tight ends coach Jason Witten to take over in interim
articles.summary: The Sooners rank No. 111 among FBS in total offense, averaging 22 points per game while going 4-4 thus far.
articles.body:
Oklahoma has fired offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle, the school confirmed on Monday .

The Sooners rank No. 111 among FBS teams in total offense at 336.9 yards per game, which is second-to-last in the SEC. In its eight games thus far, Oklahoma has averaged 22 points per game, scoring only 10 points against Michigan and 13 versus both No. 2 Georgia and No. 8 Kentucky .

Tight ends coach Jason Witten will take over as Oklahoma's interim OC and play-caller. The former Dallas Cowboys All-Pro tight end is in his first year on the Sooners' staff after five years as a high school head coach.

"I have decided to make a change at offensive coordinator. My responsibility is to the whole team and what I believe is best for us right now, " Sooners head coach Brett Venables said in a statement . "We need a change." "I believe we still have meaningful opportunities ahead and a responsibility to maximize them," he added. "Our expectations remain high and our commitment to meeting them is unwavering."

"I have decided to make a change at offensive coordinator. My responsibility is to the whole team and what I believe is best for us right now, " Sooners head coach Brett Venables said in a statement . "We need a change."

"I believe we still have meaningful opportunities ahead and a responsibility to maximize them," he added. "Our expectations remain high and our commitment to meeting them is unwavering."

Oklahoma began the 2026 season ranked No. 10 in the preseason AP Top 25 poll, but have been one of college football's biggest disappointments. Following Saturday's 42-25 loss to South Carolina, the Sooners are 4-4.

Quarterback John Mateer, who followed Arbuckle from Washington State to Oklahoma, failed to fulfill expectations as a potential Heisman Trophy candidate. In Arbuckle's offense, Mateer threw 14 touchdowns to 11 interceptions last season. This year, he's passed for 1,835 yards — 39th among FBS quarterbacks — with 13 TD passes and 7 interceptions.

Venables hired Arbuckle, 31, in December of 2024 after Seth Littrell was fired as OC during the season. With Arbuckle overseeing Washington State's offense in 2024, the Cougars averaged 36.6 points (sixth in FBS) and 442.8 yards per game (17th in FBS).

Mateer entered the transfer portal soon thereafter and committed to the Sooners. In Arbuckle's system, he threw for 3.139 yards and 29 TDs during his sophomore season for the Cougars. Mateer rushed for an additional 851 yards and 15 TDs that year.

Whomever becomes Oklahoma's next offensive coordinator will be the fifth coach to hold that position during Venable's head-coaching tenure following Jeff Lebby, Joe Jon Finley, Littrell and Arbuckle.

The remaining games on the Sooners' schedule are against No. 25 Florida, No. 12 Ole Miss, Texas A&M and No. 19 Missouri.

articles.title: JACKSON THOMPSON: Maine girls speak out about facing trans athlete as state grapples with issue
articles.summary: Two Maine high school girls describe "crushing disappointment" competing against transgender athletes as their attorney files a Title IX complaint.
articles.body: Two Maine high school girls spoke out Monday about competing against transgender athletes, describing "crushing disappointment" and urging officials to protect their opportunities as their attorney announced plans for a federal civil rights complaint. Reagan Wilson, a junior at Fryeburg Academy, and Morgan Clark, a junior and varsity soccer captain at Windham High School, addressed a news conference at the Maine State House in Augusta alongside advocates seeking a statewide vote on sex-based eligibility rules. "Many girls and women are discovering the crushing disappointment that comes from being beaten in their own sports by males who should have never been allowed to compete in the first place," Wilson said. TRANSGENDER ATHLETES HAVE TAKEN 2,293 CHAMPIONSHIP SPOTS FROM BIOLOGICAL WOMEN, NEW RESEARCH FINDS Wilson, who said she has competed in swimming, cross-country, indoor and outdoor track, soccer and softball, described facing transgender competitors across multiple seasons. "During my cross-country season, I competed against a biological male in many of my races. Most recently, I competed against a male playing on an all-girls soccer team," she said. "This is unacceptable and has deprived me and so many other girls of equal opportunity to compete and win." Clark, who said she has played soccer in Maine since she was 4, described the issue moving from something she encountered online to something affecting her own team. COLORADO SCHOOL PARENTS SOUND ALARM AFTER DAUGHTERS WERE CUT FROM VOLLEYBALL TEAM WHILE TRANS ATHLETE PLAYS "Last year, this sort of thing was something I only saw online, but now it’s something that I’m seeing in my own field," Clark said. "If it can happen to me, it can happen to you." Clark pointed to an October tie against a team whose results had improved substantially over the previous season. "In October, our team tied against a team we’ve easily outranked in past years, a team with a male athlete," she said. Windham played South Portland to a 1-1 draw on Oct. 1. The Portland Press Herald reported that South Portland finished the previous season 3-9-2 and 14th in the regional Heal point standings. A draft complaint provided to OutKick identifies a transgender player on South Portland’s girls’ soccer team as the focus of the athletes’ allegations. A scoring chart supplied for the planned complaint credited the player with 15 goals and 10 assists through South Portland’s Oct. 27 playoff game. The draft alleges that Maine’s eligibility policies deprive female athletes of equal competitive opportunities. It also describes Wilson’s previous experiences in cross-country and indoor track and field. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! At Monday’s news conference, Alliance Defending Freedom attorney Tavia Bruxellas McAlister said the organization would file a Title IX complaint that day on the girls’ behalf with the U.S. Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights. The draft seeks an investigation of the Maine Department of Education, Maine Principals’ Association, South Portland School Department and Windham Raymond School District, along with changes to eligibility policies and remedies for alleged past violations. Both Windham and South Portland were eliminated in regional semifinals Friday, ending the possibility of another meeting during this year’s playoffs. The draft says both girls intend to play varsity soccer again next year and expect to face the South Portland athlete. Maine’s policy dispute with the federal government predates the girls’ planned complaint. The Education Department announced a Title IX noncompliance finding against Maine in March 2025, and the Justice Department sued the state’s education department the following month over transgender participation in girls’ sports. Maine officials and the MPA have defended their approach by citing the Maine Human Rights Act, which protects against gender-identity discrimination. The MPA’s published policy allows transgender students to compete according to either their birth sex or gender identity, but not both. In June, the Supreme Court upheld state restrictions on transgender participation in girls’ and women’s sports. The Court expressly left unresolved whether schools may allow transgender athletes to participate on female teams, the separate question underlying Maine’s dispute. The athletes appeared as referendum organizers announced another attempt to put restrictions before Maine voters. Leyland Streiff, principal officer of the Protect Girls Sports in Maine ballot committee and a leader of Maine Girl Dads, said the group was submitting 4,836 additional signatures toward a place on the 2027 ballot. Its earlier petition fell 532 valid signatures short of qualifying for this year’s election after a legal challenge and review. Additional signatures would require state validation. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The proposal would base eligibility for designated school teams and access to bathrooms, locker rooms and other private spaces on sex recorded on students’ original birth certificates. It would also allow students to sue over qualifying violations. Clark said she hopes the effort changes the experience for her teammates and other girls. "I hope that this referendum helps girls like me and my friends play the sport that we love fairly and safely," she said.

articles.title: Matt Rhule said a Nebraska fan yelled at his 13-year-old daughter after latest loss: 'I'm not quitting'
articles.summary: Nebraska fell to Washington at home on Saturday night, marking the program's third straight loss.
articles.body:
Matt Rhule's eldest daughter was walking at Memorial Stadium on Saturday night following the Cornhuskers' 17-10 loss to Washington when a Nebraska fan walked up to her.

"F-U and F your dad," Rhule said the man told his daughter.

While Rhule confirmed on Monday that he isn't leaving his post in Lincoln, he did say that kind of behavior will drive him out of the sport completely if it keeps happening. Harassing his family, he said, is where he draws the line.

"I'm not going to keep coaching if it means my kids grow up screwed up," Rhule said, via The Athletic . "You know, I'm not going to [keep] coaching and see my daughter shook."

Rhule is in his fourth season with the Cornhuskers. He holds a 44-22 overall record at Nebraska, and he's never won more than seven games in a single season.

The Huskers have now lost three straight, and sit at 5-3 on the season entering this weekend's matchup at Illinois. They still have to go up against No. 11 Ohio State and No. 21 Iowa before the season ends, too.

Rhule still has six years left on his contract with Nebraska, too, and would be owed nearly $48 million should the university opt to fire him before the end of the year. Rhule isn't necessarily considered to be on the hot seat, and that is a very large buyout.

It's easy to understand why Nebraska fans may be frustrated with Rhule. The Cornhuskers led in the fourth quarter before allowing Washington to mount a long game-winning drive in the final minutes. That led to plenty of fans booing and things being launched down onto the field from the stands.

Rhule said he gets it, but is urging Nebraska fans to take a breath.

"This is about the people that are passionate and with us," Rhule said. "We're going to keep fighting till the day they tell me to leave. I'm not leaving. I'm not quitting. I'm fighting for those people. For the people that are listening to the game while they're on a combine. We are going to fight for those people. "But please don't ever question how hard these kids are working or how hard these coaches are working or how hard I'm working."

"This is about the people that are passionate and with us," Rhule said. "We're going to keep fighting till the day they tell me to leave. I'm not leaving. I'm not quitting. I'm fighting for those people. For the people that are listening to the game while they're on a combine. We are going to fight for those people.

"But please don't ever question how hard these kids are working or how hard these coaches are working or how hard I'm working."

As for his family, Rhule said they are all still on board, too. Rhule's oldest son, Bryant, is a college student at Nebraska and has done work with the football team. Rhule's 10-year-old daughter texted him in the wake of the loss.

"She was like: 'Dad, I love Nebraska. I love living in Nebraska. I love Nebraska football. I love the players. I'm tough. This is just teaching me life lessons. Please don't quit,'" he said.

articles.title: Arrasate: "Es una derrota muy dolorosa"
articles.standfirst: El técnico de Osasuna cree que a su equipo le faltó tener más balón
articles.summary: El técnico de Osasuna cree que a su equipo le faltó tener más balón
articles.body: El entrenador de Osasuna, Jagoba Arrasate, calificó de "muy dolorosa" la derrota de su equipo ante el Deportivo, que remontó con un gol de Nsongo Bil en el minuto 87 el tanto de Budimir en el primer tiempo. "Creo que hemos empezado mal, con un par de regalos donde Sergio creo que ha estado brillante y nos ha mantenido en el partido. A partir de ahí, hemos ido creciendo y hemos hecho el gol en una presión alta. Creo que hemos terminado bien el primer tiempo", analizó. "Sabíamos que el Dépor en la segunda parte nos iba a achuchar, que tenía cambios para cambiar el guion del partido y creo que el gol otra vez nos hace mucho daño porque es un balón que tenemos controlado en el centro del campo, la perdemos, una falta un poco dudosa y Soriano hace el gol", continuó. En rueda de prensa, el técnico vizcaíno dijo que, tras el 1-1, a su equipo le faltó "tener más balón, tener más secuencias para poder defender mejor" porque se hundieron demasiado. "Al final, cuando estás defendiendo tanto tiempo… Adama hace una buena acción individual, un buen centro y el gol. Para nosotros es una derrota muy dolorosa. Fuera de casa, el otro día encajamos dos, hoy otra vez dos. Además, hoy con el agravante de que hemos empezado ganando el partido y necesitamos ser más sólidos fuera de casa porque, si no, es muy difícil puntuar", subrayó.

articles.title: La clave del nuevo Madrid está donde nadie la esperaba
articles.standfirst: El equipo blanco encuentra el equilibrio con el balón y Mou empieza a ver cómo sus ideas calan en el vestuario
articles.summary: El equipo blanco encuentra el equilibrio con el balón y Mou empieza a ver cómo sus ideas calan en el vestuario
articles.body: La mejoría defensiva del Real Madrid empieza a ser cada vez más evidente y tiene mucho que ver con su evolución con el balón. En Valdebebas perciben un equipo más seguro, que controla mejor los partidos, pierde menos posesiones y está más preparado para reaccionar cuando las pierde. El Madrid está encontrando una fórmula que empieza a dar resultados y que encierra una paradoja interesante. Atacar mejor le está permitiendo defender mejor. El Madrid gestiona mejor los ritmos, falla muchos menos pases y concede menos facilidades a sus rivales para recuperar la posesión. Ya no es un equipo tan anárquico en ataque y eso tiene una consecuencia directa cuando pierde el balón: sus jugadores están mejor colocados para activar la presión tras pérdida, reaccionar rápidamente e intentar recuperar la posesión lejos de su portería. Ahí el tridente de Mou (Diomande, Bellingham y Arda) está siendo clave para darle sentido a todo. Pero la evolución no se limita a esa primera reacción. Una de las señales más positivas que observan en Valdebebas es que el equipo también empieza a sentirse cómodo cuando no consigue recuperar inmediatamente. El Madrid muestra más orden en defensa organizada, cierra mejor los espacios interiores y mantiene mayor compactación entre sus líneas. Es decir, no necesita robar siempre rápido para evitar que el rival le haga daño. Ante el Racing, por ejemplo, permitió un solo disparo a puerta. Detrás de esta evolución táctica también hay una cuestión de entendimiento entre Mourinho y sus futbolistas. El propio entrenador dejó una reflexión muy significativa después de la victoria: "Yo entendiendo cosas que no entendía el primer día, los jugadores entienden mejor mi carácter como entrenador. Entienden las cosas que para mí no son negociables, existe una buena empatía humana, jugadores-entrenador, mis ideas y sus calidades...". Una declaración que refleja que el proceso de adaptación avanza y que sus exigencias empiezan a calar en el vestuario. Ahora se aprecia un equipo más compacto, con menos desajustes y que comprende cada vez mejor cómo quiere jugar su entrenador. La maquinaria defensiva todavía está lejos del nivel de perfección que pretende Mou, pero la tendencia es positiva. Ahí, las largas posesiones y la calma que se está teniendo en la base apunta a una de las claves de la mejoría blanca, que se está protegiendo de la manera que nadie la esperaba... con balón.

articles.title: Troy Deeney's Team of the Week: Rice, Konsa, Van Hecke, McBurnie
articles.summary: After every round of Premier League matches this season, Troy Deeney gives us his team of the week. Do you agree with his choices?
articles.body:
After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.

Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

Bart Verbruggen (Brighton): He was unreal. Lots of saves which kept Brighton in it, even the last-ditch save where it hit him in the face.

Just an impenetrable wall. Brighton should really have lost by two or three goals, but Verbruggen was the reason they didn't.

Archie Gray (Tottenham): I'm going with a fully north London back four. Gray scored and defended really well. He was under a lot of pressure when Tottenham were in bad form and got a lot of stick, but now Spurs are starting to pick up I'm going to give him a bit of credit.

Ezri Konsa (Arsenal): He was a beast. Head it, kick it, throw your body in front of the ball. He defended and fought for the team, getting the job done.

Jan Paul van Hecke (Tottenham): Van Hecke got a goal and he's really growing into his role at Spurs. I still think he was a little bit overpriced, but all in all he's had a solid start, coming up with a few goals. Micky van de Ven next to him gives him confidence that he can go and be really aggressive, because Van der Ven will cover him with his pace.

Jurrien Timber (Arsenal): Timber got away with a shirt pull on Alexander Isak and I'm really surprised the ref and video assistant referee (VAR) didn't look at it. But again I thought he recovered and defended really well at full-back.

Romeo Lavia (Chelsea): I thought Lavia was excellent for Chelsea. People will turn to Manchester United having 10 men, but the 60 minutes before that Chelsea were all over the place. Lavia was the only constant breaking up play, keeping the ball moving. Plus he had an assist.

Declan Rice (Arsenal): A proper captain's performance, he gets the job done all over the pitch. He got a little assist for himself, too.

Tatsuhiro Sakamoto (Coventry): Sakamoto goes unnoticed by a lot of people, but I think he works really hard for the team and he is very humble in his approach. On Saturday he also delivered in a massive game for his team.

Johan Manzambi (Aston Villa): Another assist for him. He's a 21-year-old who is just flying. His confidence is through the roof and he is taking over this Villa team. Really good player, only going to get better. He was taken off thinking about the Champions League game against Barcelona, but up until that point Fulham couldn't really stop him.

Ollie McBurnie (Hull): Grafter, scrappy, endeavour, goals, assists... He had it all in his game.

He epitomises what Hull are: a player that's always overlooked, a team that's always overlooked, but they've got some spirit, some fight.

Taiwo Awoniyi (Coventry): Unbelievable solo goal. It's really good to see the big fella back playing and being in a situation where he can impose himself. If Coventry are to stay up, he's going to be why.

Frank Lampard (Coventry): He has been really good. Coventry have taken care of business against Sunderland, it's a massive six-pointer those games and his team came out front-footed, aggressive and also did a job on a very good Sunderland team.

Also a massive nod to Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta for getting the job done at Liverpool.

articles.title: Jack Grealish can still have Everton future, says David Moyes
articles.summary: Everton boss David Moyes says there is a way back for Jack Grealish at the club - but does not know when he might return to the team.
articles.body:
Everton boss David Moyes says there is a way back for Jack Grealish at the club - but does not know when he will return to the team.

The former England midfielder missed both of the Toffees' wins over Newcastle in the past week after a disciplinary issue.

The 31-year-old Manchester City loanee was left out of Thursday's 3-1 victory in the Carabao Cup - a decision made by the club - after what was thought to be an unauthorised absence from training.

And again on Monday for their Premier League meeting - which Everton won 1-0 at St James' Park with Thierno Barry scoring the only goal - Grealish was absent.

The Toffees said it was because of a lack of fitness - but Moyes was very coy at full-time.

"He's unavailable at the moment and we will make a decision with the club when we think that availability comes back," he told BBC Sport.

When asked whether it was indeed related to fitness, he added: "All I'm giving out is that he is unavailable at the moment."

And when pressed over whether the disciplinary issue is over with, Moyes said: "No, I can't comment on that."

Everton 's next match is at home to Coventry on Friday (20:00 GMT) with Moyes unsure whether Grealish will be available then.

But when asked if there was a way back for him at the club, Moyes said: "Of course there is."

Grealish is trying to rebuild his career at Everton , having fallen out of favour at City despite costing the club £100m in 2021.

Grealish, who played a key role helping City win the 2022-23 Treble, will be out of contract at the end of the season.

He scored twice in 22 games for Everton last season during a loan spell which was cut short by injury.

The midfielder returned to the club for a second loan spell this season but had only made six appearances before falling out of favour.

articles.title: Tottenham Hotspur star at risk of suspension as North London Derby approaches
articles.summary: Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Conor Gallagher is walking a Premier League disciplinary tightrope and could miss the North London Derby against Arsenal if he p...
articles.body:
Conor Gallagher could be heading toward a period on the sidelines. The Tottenham Hotspur midfielder will navigate a precarious disciplinary situation over the next several weeks, having accumulated his share of yellow cards this campaign, placing him in danger of a one-match suspension.

Gallagher has already collected three bookings in the Premier League, while Mateus Fernandes, Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, and Micky van de Ven have been cautioned twice. According to The FA's regulations, players who accumulate five yellow cards within the opening 19 fixtures of the season serve a one-game suspension.

Should a player receive 10 bookings during the initial 32 Premier League games, they face a two-match ban. While Roberto De Zerbi should possess sufficient depth to cover for the England international's temporary unavailability, he'll prefer having his strongest players ready for selection when the Lilywhites meet Arsenal next month.

Should Gallagher pick up a yellow card in any of the upcoming three Premier League fixtures – Leeds United (A) on Saturday, November 7, Ipswich Town (H) on Saturday, November 21, or Sunderland (A) on Sunday, November 29 – followed by another caution when Spurs welcome Fulham on Thursday, December 3, he'll be absent for the North London Derby on Sunday, December 6.

The 26-year-old midfielder could, though, complete the suspension ahead of the Gunners fixture by picking up his fifth booking before Tottenham meet the Cottagers, as per football.london .

Aston Villa's Matty Cash and Hull City's Matt Crooks have already accumulated five yellow cards this campaign; both will serve their suspensions this weekend.

Brentford's Vitaly Janelt and Igor Thiago, Brighton and Hove Albion's Pascal Groß, Hull City's Oliver McBurnie, Leeds United's Ethan Ampadu, and Manchester United's Harry Maguire are all treading on thin ice with four cautions apiece.

Gallagher, alongside Fernandes, Gray, Van Hecke, and Van de Ven, must exercise caution until matchday 19, scheduled from Friday, January 1, through Sunday, January 3, when the booking threshold for a suspension rises from five to 10.

Meanwhile, Spurs are scheduled to take on Arsenal, Liverpool, Brighton, and Manchester City. Despite the former Chelsea player having made limited appearances this season, with only three Premier League starts to his name, he has captured De Zerbi's attention.

Shortly after the Italian assumed control back in April, he voiced his appreciation for Gallagher. De Zerbi said: "I want to see again the same Gallagher I loved in Chelsea at the time."

He added: "I think for Gallagher it's not so easy because he left Chelsea after I don't know how many seasons. He went to Atlético Madrid, and now in Tottenham, in this moment for Tottenham.

"He was a leader in Chelsea, and now he has to adapt to a new club, to new teammates, to a new stadium, to a new everything. I have to help him to put as a target the Gallagher in Chelsea."

Several weeks later, after a 2-1 victory over Aston Villa that lifted them clear of the drop zone, De Zerbi remarked: "When Gallagher plays like this, we play with 12 players because you can find him as a striker, as a midfielder, as a full-back - everywhere on the pitch you can find him. Great player, great passion, great qualities."

articles.title: Ashley Sanchez’s ‘Incredible’ 2026 Has Her Setting Goal-Scoring Records and Planning a Wedding: ‘It’s Been Amazing’
articles.summary: The emerging North Carolina Courage star recently tied the NWSL single-season record for goals and has a chance to break the mark this weekend
articles.body:
It would be safe to say 2026 has exceeded all of Ashley Sanchez' s goals ... pun intended.

Just months after announcing her engagement to fellow professional soccer player Tommy Williamson, the North Carolina Courage striker finds herself at the end of a historic season, tying the National Women's Soccer League scoring record (set by Temwa Chawinga in 2024) and winning the Golden Boot .

"It's been amazing," Sanchez, 27, told PEOPLE before her final game of the season against the Denver Summit. "It's definitely been a really crazy experience. I don't think it will hit me until the season's over and I've really reflected on everything, but it's been really incredible. I'm really proud of how I've been able to have the year that I have."

Sanchez's engagement isn't the only way her fiancé contributed to her incredible 2026: He also suggested one day while they trained together that she switch positions on the field.

The career midfielder decided to be uncharacteristically receptive to his suggestion. "Sometimes I can be a little demanding when we train and it's not the best for the relationship," the Pasadena, Calif., native says with a laugh. "But I was good this off-season, and I was open to suggestions."

Soon, Sanchez realized Williamson's off-the-cuff idea opened up a new world for her on the pitch: more one-versus-one situations, and more chances to shoot. In preseason training camps, Courage head coach Mak Lind took notice of his midfielder's new pep and solidified her to left wing.

The change has paid off: This season, Sanchez's 20 goals in 30 games earned her the award given to the highest goal-scorer in the league each season.

"I'm not really sure why my fiancé thought of that this summer, but I mean, honestly, it worked out," Sanchez says. "He really seems like a genius right now."

But the truth is, Sanchez has always been a goal scorer.

Growing up in Los Angeles County, she first fell in love with soccer when her parents, Ralph and Julie, signed her up for a local league at 3 years old.

"I was pretty good already and it's always easier to enjoy something when you feel like you're better than people," Sanchez jokes, telling stories about other kids being more interested in "picking flowers" while she was laser-focused on the net. "I would just dribble around them and score. I really loved playing, it felt natural."

By the time Sanchez was in eighth grade, she had already secured a scholarship to play soccer at UCLA. In college, Sanchez broke records for assists as a midfielder with scoring on the back burner, and began to come to the realization soccer could be her post-college career as well.

"It's crazy because growing up, I didn't even really know that there was a pathway to play professional soccer for women," she says. "I just really enjoyed playing, and I didn't think too far into the future about it."

Sanchez, who now also plays on the U.S. Women's National Soccer Team , adds: "[My soccer career] was definitely for just how much I enjoyed playing, and I still feel that way."

After three seasons at UCLA, Sanchez was drafted by the Washington Spirit in 2020 and made her professional debut at 21. She helped lead the Spirit to its first and only NWSL Championship in 2021 before being traded to North Carolina after the next season. But no year has compared to Sanchez's 2026 season, emerging as one of the sport's premier goal scorers.

Off the field, Sanchez jokes that she's "so lazy," using her time away from the pitch to "just chill" and take her mind off the sport.

She and Williamson, whom she met on a blind double date while they both played soccer for their respective pro teams in North Carolina, enjoying walking their two dogs together (Benny, a 2-year-old yellow lab, and Nala, a 4-year-old French bulldog). "They're just really some funny characters," she says.

She's also tried crocheting ("way too difficult for me") while working on taming her "shopping addiction" with more at-home hobbies. But ultimately, it all comes back to the pitch for her.

"You kind of get into that flow state and it kind of feels like things are just working out for you, which is always nice," Sanchez says about her record-setting performance this season. "I think I've just been putting myself in the best possible situations, and so far it's been working."

Though the Courage won their Sunday game against the Summit, they were knocked out of playoff contention by Seattle's victory over Orlando. The NSWL playoffs begin Nov. 6.

articles.body:
Utah is now 8-0 on the year and is looking to make a run to the College Football Playoff. Utah has jumped into the Top 5 in the AP Poll and is heading into the biggest stretch of the season.

This Saturday, Utah will host BYU in a Top 10 matchup. As they head into the game, the Utes will be without one of their top players , per Pete Thamel of ESPN.

"Morgan Scalley announces that Utah freshman starting offensive lineman Kelvin Obot (lower leg) is out for the year. He's a former 5-star recruit at offensive tackle who was a Top 50 overall recruit and a Top 5 tackle recruit. He'd started three games at guard for Utah this year," Thamel posted on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Obot left the game with Colorado after being rolled up on during a run by Wayshawn Parker against Colorado. He missed the game against Cincinnati this past weekend, and now is out of the lineup. Head coach Morgan Scalley understands the implications of one of his top offensive linemen being out of the lineup, per Jason Batacao of The Salt Lake Tribune.

"We've got BYU coming up, huge matchup," Scalley said. "I believe it's the first time that we've both been in the top 10 going up against each other. It's awesome, awesome for the state. Big rivalry game. Kalani, respect the heck out of him."

BYU and Utah have faced off 97 times previously. BYU has won three straight in the series, but Utah leads the series 59-24-4. The top-ten matchup between BYU and Utah is set for noon ET on Saturday.

articles.title: Thierno Barry's revival: From nightmare debut season to Everton hero
articles.summary: Last season Thierno Barry scored eight goals in 41 appearances. This season it's taken him just 12 games to match that tally.
articles.body:
Last season Thierno Barry scored eight goals in 41 appearances.

This season it's taken him just 12 games to match that tally.

On Monday night Barry scored against Newcastle for the second time in five days as his side earned a deserved win at St James' Park in the Premier League.

Only Erling Haaland (13) has scored more goals among Premier League players in all competitions this season than Barry (eight).

The 24-year-old is on his best run of form since joining the club from Villarreal last summer and, as Everton 's only recognised senior striker following Beto's transfer to Fiorentina, is currently indispensable to the Toffees.

By scoring once again Barry highlighted why Everton paid £27m for a striker who grew up watching Wayne Rooney and Romelu Lukaku score for the Toffees.

The Frenchman had a rough start to life on Merseyside, having just one shot across his first 16 Everton games, and last month posted a video of himself breaking down during a private training session last season.

That moment was contrasted by his celebration on Monday night, which started with a knee slide and ended with dance moves.

"I was working a lot during the summer and now we can see the result," Barry told Sky Sports.

"The season is long but I'm happy to help the team with my goals.

"I want to enjoy more than last season and I enjoyed my celebration so I am happy."

It was a controversial strike though with Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle telling BBC Sport there was "a clear foul on Fabian Schar" in the build-up.

Who produced the kind of performance Moyes loves? - player ratings

Barry cements himself as Everton's main man

In the Premier League Barry leads the way for being involved in the highest proportion of his team's big chances.

Before Monday's match, Everton had recorded 24 big chances, and Barry had been involved in 15 of them (62.5%).

The striker has often been criticised for being wasteful in front of goal.

In Monday's match, for instance, he latched on to Jarrad Branthwaite's flick-on but, when through on goal, made a poor connection with the ball and scuffed his shot.

His goal - a tap-in from two yards - was very difficult not to convert, with the opportunity having had an incredibly high xG of 0.995.

"We know Barry misses chances, but we also know this season he keeps going and he scores goals," former Liverpool and England defender Jamie Carragher told Sky Sports.

His manager David Moyes added: "We're thrilled he's getting the goals because you need your centre-forward to score. He has missed a few but thankfully tonight he was on the spot to get the goal."

articles.title: Everton beat disappointing Newcastle as Ramsey sees late red
articles.summary: Reaction as Newcastle beaten by Everton in Premier League and jeered off by home fans.
articles.body:
Thierno Barry scored against Newcastle for the second time in five days as his Everton side eased to a narrow win at St James' Park in the Premier League.

Tyrique George was allowed to run into the box unmarked and his low shot got underneath Newcastle keeper Lukas Hornicek before it was tapped in by Barry from a few yards out in the 49th minute.

Barry's finish was his eighth goal in 12 games across all competitions this season and backed up his strike in Everton's 3-1 Carabao Cup win over Newcastle on Thursday.

Newcastle's fortunes were made worse in the 98th minute when midfielder Jacob Ramsey was shown a second yellow card, 84 seconds after receiving his first, for catching Harrison Armstrong above the Everton player's ankle.

Everton were the better side on a rainy Monday night and almost added a second through Jarrad Branthwaite's header, which was saved smartly midway through the second half.

The visitors also had a late penalty shout when Fabian Schar appeared to catch Barry in the box as he attempted a clearance, but the video assistant referee upheld referee John Brooks' no-penalty call.

Newcastle's best chance of a leveller came in the 66th minute when Anthony Elanga met Harvey Barnes' cross with a powerful shot which was saved by a combination of Jordan Pickford and the post, before briefly trickling along the goalline.

England goalkeeper Pickford also did well to keep out substitute Yoane Wissa's low effort with his feet in the 90th minute.

But Newcastle were otherwise second best as Barry's goal inspired Everton to their first league win since September.

Everton's double-header against Newcastle has gone well on the pitch, but off it headlines had been dominated by the club's call to drop Manchester City loanee Jack Grealish.

The England midfielder was not in Everton's squad for Thursday's win because of a "breach of club discipline" and he was again not included on Monday.

Everton have not disclosed any further details, but the decision is understood to have arisen from an unauthorised absence from training.

With midfielders Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Merlin Rohl stepping up, it might be difficult for Grealish to win his place back in the starting XI.

Consecutive wins have put Everton back on track after back-to-back 2-0 losses to Chelsea and Arsenal, which followed a draw at Hull.

Moyes' team are clicking and they are up to seventh in the Premier League table, two points behind fifth-placed Liverpool.

Newcastle are 13th in the Premier League table and seriously out of form, with four defeats from their past five games in all competitions.

And a lot of their struggles have come at St James' Park, where they have only won one of their five league matches this season and are yet to keep a clean sheet.

Newcastle's defenders were caught napping for Everton's opener, allowing a free George to drive into the box before he unleashed a shot which should have been handled better by keeper Hornicek.

Nobody was close to Barry, who tapped in on the rebound.

Going forward the home side were poor for the first hour before a late flurry of chances as they pushed for an equaliser.

They will be without Ramsey for their next match, away to Fulham on Saturday (15:00 GMT), after the midfielder was dismissed for a poor challenge on the halfway line - seconds after being booked for a late tackle on Hayden Hackney.

Ramsey and his team-mates were booed off by pockets of their supporters at both half-time and full-time, with their side four points above the bottom three.
